- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/08/11 (Fri) 00:49
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] HTML DOM and Browser BOM are two distinct models that make up the core of web development.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The HTML DOM (Document Object Model) is a programming interface that allows developers to manipulate the content and structure of a web page using code.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The HTML DOM represents the web page as a hierarchical tree of objects, where each object corresponds to an element, attribute, or text node in the HTML document.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] With the HTML DOM, developers can dynamically modify the contents of a web page, respond to user interactions, and create dynamic effects and animations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Browser BOM (Browser Object Model) is a programming interface that allows developers to manipulate the behavior and appearance of the web browser itself.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Browser BOM provides access to browser-specific features such as the history, location, and navigation properties, as well as the ability to create pop-up windows, display dialogs, and manipulate the browser's status bar.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Examples of the HTML DOM and Browser BOM include dynamically adding or removing elements from a web page based on user input and navigating to a different URL or displaying a pop-up window when a user clicks a button.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] `onclick()` is an event handler that can be used to execute a piece of JavaScript code when an element is clicked.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The `onclick()` event handler can be attached to any HTML element, such as a button, link, or image, using the `onclick` attribute.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Example of `onclick()`: `<button onclick="alert('Hello, world!')">Click me</button>`.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] `onclick()` is just one of many event handlers available in the HTML DOM event model, including `onmouseover`, `onmouseout`, and `onsubmit`.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] `onload()` is an event handler that is used to execute a piece of JavaScript code when a web page has finished loading.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The `onload()` event handler can be attached to the `window` object or any HTML element using the `onload` attribute.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Example of `onload()`: `<body onload="alert('Page loaded!')">`.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The `onload()` event handler is commonly used to perform actions that require the web page or its content to be fully loaded.
